questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of Work Done?
questions.answer: Work measures the energy transferred by a force through a displacement. Only the component of force along the displacement contributes to work. For a constant force, work is a dot product. For a force that changes along a path, work is a line integral of force along the path.

questions.prompt: What does \(W\) mean in Work Done?
questions.answer: In Work Done, \(W\) means work done by a force. Its unit is J.

questions.prompt: Identify another important piece of notation used in Work Done.
questions.answer: In Work Done, \(\mathbf F\) means force. Its unit is N.

questions.prompt: State a central formula or test for Work Done.
questions.answer:
The constant-force work is
\[W=\mathbf F\cdot\Delta\mathbf r\]

questions.prompt: A constant force of magnitude \(10\) N acts at angle \(60^\circ\) to a \(4\) m displacement. Find the work.
questions.answer: Use the dot-product form \(W=|\mathbf F||\Delta\mathbf r|\cos\theta\). Substitute \(|\mathbf F|=10\), \(|\Delta\mathbf r|=4\), and \(\cos60^\circ=1/2\): \(W=10\cdot4\cdot\frac12=20\) J.

questions.prompt: A constant force \(\mathbf F=3\mathbf i+4\mathbf j\) N moves a particle by \(\Delta\mathbf r=2\mathbf i\) m. Find the work.
questions.answer: Use the dot product: \(W=(3\mathbf i+4\mathbf j)\cdot(2\mathbf i)=6\) J. The \(\mathbf j\) component does not contribute because the displacement has no \(\mathbf j\) component.

questions.prompt: A force is opposite to displacement. What is the sign of the work?
questions.answer: The angle between force and displacement is \(\pi\), so \(\cos\pi=-1\). The dot product is negative, so the work is negative.
